Results.ReviewText:
Super efficient and great alternative to traditional charcoal kettle grill. I have the large Weber charcoal grill and have been using it for years. I cook burgers, dogs, fish and shrimp direct and also use it for long low and slow cooks of ribs chicken and brisket.  Only issue is that it takes awhile for the grill to get ready and it’s not ideal for a quick on the go on last minute feed. We bought this gas grill as an alternative for times when we want something quick and delicious but do not have the time to go through all the steps a charcoal grill requires.  This grill gets nice and hot fast.  Yes you do not get the same high high heat as a charcoal grill or the all the smoky flavor but for foods that to me rely more on seasoning like a great burger or things without A lot of fat like a piece of swordfish this grill is perfect.  My only wish is that there was a way to flame kiss some
Of the food.  Hot dogs can tend to taste a little more fried than grilled as the fat does not render in the same way as it does over charcoal.  Still decisions but my preference is to have a lot of char. But many guests and family like it orher wise.  I say get this grill if you want quick and easy and dependable performance.  Much simpler and less to worry about than charcoal. You will love it.  I’m just a grill snob who cooks on charcoal when he can. Lol.
Results.Title: Awesome alternative to charcoal grill!

Results.ReviewText:
Whenever I hope to connect with the countless generations which came before me, forgotten and unknown - stretching into the past, I try to focus on whatever genuine pleasures we share. 

Pleasures before literacy. 

Pre-literate pleasure.  
Before any faint scent of epistemology could enter one's consciousness other than through a proximate contemporary. A history derived completely from the anecdotal.

What united us? 
What united our forbears, huddled together against the cold and certain death from predators, real and imagined, longing for safety.

What brought joy to those who genetically dwell in me, though separated by the millennia, pleasure?

Sex? Undoubtedly. 

A stomach filled with nourishment? Surely.

But fire. 


Now fire.

A hearth. A communal hearth.

Warmth.

Safety?

A sure way of warding off the superstitious and real threats of the night.

The smell of roasted meat (which drew the superior beings, known as dogs, to strike a selfish bargain with our species from which we have profited since its inception) giving our progenitors fits of ecstasy from the flame-kissed smells and tastes. 

Drawing together.



As I come home from work and ponder the complex nature of existence and my righteous and unrighteous complaints regarding modern life, I take warm comfort in communion with my ancestors.

I can't fix everything.

But I can grill a pretty fierce zucchini.

I may be elderly and unable to synthesize poison from natural ingredients and anneal it to a homemade dart in order to expel it from a blowgun into an unsuspecting eland and subsequently run it down over miles and drag it back home to the communal hearth, but I can delight my wife and family with a variety of evenly cooked meats on an autumn eve, toasting those that came before me with joy and fellowship across the years.

Thanks Weber.
